chunks: He has enjoined upon himself justice.
The first step of his justice is the rejection of desires from his self; he describes the truth and acts according to it.
There is no good which he has not aimed at, nor any likely place (of virtue) which he has not sought.
He has given the Book control over his rein, so it is his guide and his leader.
He settles where the Book settles and descends where the Book descends.
ai.seo_question: What are the key characteristics of a faithful believer according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this passage from Nahj al-Balagha outlines the spiritual architecture of the 'Adil' (just) believer, where self-mastery over *hawa* (caprice) is the prerequisite for divine justice. It portrays the Quran not merely as a text but as an active, guiding companion ('Thaqalayn'), reflecting the Shi'a emphasis on the inseparability of scripture and the Ahl al-Bayt as dual sources of guidance. This description aligns with the concept of *Ihsan*, where internal purity manifests as consistent external action.
